paragraphs.source_en: 10 (p. 29) Grimalkin: A term for an old she-cat, “Grimalkin” can also be a derogative expression for an old woman or hag. “Gray malkin” is the name of one of the familiars, or spirits, that serve the Witches in Macbeth (act 1, scene 1). Lockwood’s remark, at the end of the previous paragraph, that “a brindled, grey cat . . . saluted me with a querulous mew” echoes Macbeth: “Thrice the brinded cat hath mewed” (act 4, scene 1).
